title: Desktop releases install from one signed, notarized universal dmg and update from per-arch zips; publish checks the app in every artifact; one release date; the packaged app ships with Electron fuses hardened and refuses remote-debugging switches; agents attach only to their own debug run
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test packages/desktop/tracy-desktop/test/release.test.mjs packages/desktop/tracy-desktop/test/release-preflight.test.mjs packages/desktop/tracy-desktop/test/updater.test.mjs packages/desktop/tracy-desktop/test/attach.test.mjs packages/desktop/tracy-desktop/test/fuses.test.mjs packages/desktop/tracy-desktop/test/debug-switches.test.mjs
S2: Read the pass/fail counts and the named tests below.
expect: Prepare builds arm64 + x64 + universal by default: two zips for updates and one universal dmg; --arch narrows to one chip; a universal zip, a chip without its zip, a missing universal dmg, or a dmg that is not a notarized, stapled Developer ID image is refused before anything is uploaded.
The ad-hoc download link prefers the universal dmg.

Publish opens the app inside every zip and dmg and judges each in its own signature line, including the binary arch and, for a dmg, the image itself; an app that cannot be opened fails on a real store and is not checked on a test target.
Prepare freezes one releaseDate for the manifest, the frozen channel file and release.sh; a manifest whose frozen file carries another date is refused.
Attaching to a running debug run needs a live pid, the asked origin and a loopback debug port held by that pid; every refusal names its reason.

A packaged app's Electron fuses are hardened in every arch slice (RunAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS and --inspect off, cookie encryption on); flipping an .app hardens its framework binary; publish fails an artifact whose app is not hardened, naming the fuse.
A packaged app refuses --remote-debugging-port/-pipe/-address in any spelling as main.js's first act (a source run keeps them); publish fails an artifact whose main.js lost that guard.
fence: prepare's artifact rules and dmg container check; preflight's per-artifact signature lines; readManifest's release date; attachDecision; fuseProblems over every fuse wire; refusedDebugSwitch and debugGuardFirst

tests: prepare builds both archs and a universal dmg by default: two zips for updates, one dmg to install
--arch narrows the build: one arch makes no universal app, and its own zip and dmg
prepare refuses a build whose artifacts would confuse the updater: a universal zip, or an arch with no zip
prepare uploads nothing when a dmg it built is not notarized and stapled as an image
the download page prefers the universal dmg: one file that runs on either chip
every artifact of a release has its app checked, each in a line of its own
an app whose binary is not the artifact's arch fails: an x64 zip holding arm64, a universal dmg holding one arch
a dmg is judged as a container too: Developer ID signed, notarized and stapled, or its line fails
publish checks the app inside EVERY artifact — both zips and the universal dmg — each against its arch
where the apps cannot be opened (no macOS), a test target says "not checked" and a real store refuses
an artifact whose app will not open is a FAIL line of its own, and the other checks still run
prepare freezes ONE release date: the build (release.sh) gets the date the frozen channel file carries
a manifest whose frozen channel file carries another date than the manifest is refused
a live run of the asked origin, with its own loopback debug port, may be attached
each reason to refuse is named
every fuse wire in a binary is read: one for an arch binary, two for a universal one
a universal binary passes only when BOTH slices are hardened
flipping an .app hardens its framework binary — the path package.sh hands over
an app whose Electron fuses are not hardened fails its signature line, naming the fuse
a packaged app refuses every remote-debugging switch, in every spelling
a source run keeps them, and a packaged app with none starts
main.js refuses the switches before anything else runs — before app.whenReady
an app whose main.js does not refuse remote-debugging switches first fails its signature line
a universal dmg listed off the feed is never preferred over this arch on the feed
